version.changelog: Session pools: calls on one target run side by side over HTTPS (HLD §16 D-13(2)); needs vmware-policy 1.22.0.

llm.summary: This is a coherent read-only VMware log-search skill, with disclosed local credential/config storage that users should protect carefully.

dimensions.detail: The skill needs network access to the configured Log Insight appliance and reads potentially sensitive operational logs, which is proportionate to its purpose but should use a least-privilege read-only account.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses a versioned uv package and creates a user config directory under ~/.vmware-log-insight; the artifact does not include hidden install hooks, cron jobs, or startup services.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The routing instructions are scoped to VMware/vSphere/ESXi log investigations and explicitly say not to use the skill for unrelated vCenter alarms, metrics, or non-Log-Insight tasks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It discloses local persistent config, a .env password file, base64 obfuscation on first load, and an audit database at ~/.vmware/audit.db; these are purpose-aligned and disclosed, not hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is VMware Log Insight search, aggregation, field discovery, and alert-history lookup; the documented MCP surface is seven read-only tools with no ingest, edit, delete, or alert-management capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the agent read access to VMware Log Insight data. Use a read-only service account, keep the .env file out of repositories and backups where possible, prefer a secret manager for production passwords, keep TLS verification enabled outside labs, and expose the MCP server over HTTPS only with tight network access and bearer-token management.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: Credential handling is real because the tool must authenticate to Log Insight, but the artifacts disclose the .env path, warn that b64 is obfuscation rather than encryption, and recommend secret-manager injection for stronger secrecy.
[TM1] expected: The flagged --skip-auth option is documented only for the doctor diagnostic command, not as a default runtime mode or a way to bypass MCP bearer-token controls.
[TM3] expected: The same --skip-auth diagnostic flag is not an unsafe default; normal verification includes authentication, and TLS verification is documented as enabled by default.
[RA2] expected: The flagged local config directory and audit database are disclosed state files for configuration and auditing; I found no artifact evidence of cron jobs, startup scripts, backdoors, or unauthorized background persistence.
[PE2] expected: The chmod 600 references are file-permission hardening for the credential file, not sudo/root execution or privilege escalation.
